summary: Medisphere Health private deployment: control-plane upgrade omitted audit-log entries, causing transcript and session-replay loss — major incident & post-incident action plan
description:
Issue summary:
During a control-plane upgrade for Medisphere Health's private VPC deployment in eu-central on 2026-03-10, the audit-log emitter process failed to rotate and re-subscribe to the internal changefeed. As a result a window of ~27 minutes of audit entries (including transcript and session-replay metadata) were not written to the customer-managed audit store.

Impact:
- Transcript segments and session replay artifacts for completion and streaming requests were missing for a subset of customer sessions (approx 3.2k requests).
- Medisphere reported inability to perform required regulatory reconstruction for 11 patient-interaction sessions during the window.
- Customer observed elevated error rates for session-replay retrieval (404) and filed a P0 escalation.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) with Redwood private control plane in eu-central region.
- Deployment mode: private (customer provided audit sink via S3-compatible endpoint behind presigned URLs).

Steps to reproduce (high-level):
1) Triggered rolling upgrade of control-plane components (2026-03-10 09:12 UTC) using canary-first strategy.
2) During leader handoff, audit-emitter pod failed liveness probe and was restarted twice due to a transient TLS handshake failure with the customer's audit sink endpoint.
3) Restart sequence omitted the final subscription acknowledgement to the internal changefeed; component considered the window handled and did not rehydrate outgoing audit buffer.
4) Replay requests for sessions whose finalization occurred during 2026-03-10 09:18–09:45 UTC returned 404 for audit artifacts.

Logs/Snapshots:
- Control-plane logs: /logs/control-plane/2026-03-10/upgrade-run-09:12 (attached to ticket).
- Audit-emitter stacktrace: emitter_restart_2026-03-10.txt.
- Customer error samples and request IDs: [req-6c9f2, req-6c9f3, req-6c9fe ...]

Customer impact and regulatory note:
Medisphere is an enterprise healthcare customer subject to regional data retention and reconstruction requirements. Missing audit entries triggered an urgent compliance review. They requested an immediate remediation plan, forensic artifact delivery, and assurance that this window will be reconstructable where possible.

Initial mitigation performed:
- On-disk audit buffers were recovered from the control-plane node snapshots for the affected canary (eu-central-ctl-5). Partial artifacts were reconstructed and delivered to Medisphere under secure transfer.
- Rolling upgrade halted and a safety flag (safe-audit-restart) was added to the release job.
- Customer granted temporary elevated access for SRE to replay buffered events to their sink; replay jobs applied with explicit idempotency checks.

Why this is unique/different from previous incidents:
- This incident involved a private audit sink (customer-managed) combined with TLS handshake eccentricities during leader re-election. The interplay between emitter restart behavior and changefeed subscription semantics produced a silent omission (no 5xx) rather than a hard failure, increasing time-to-detect.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:55 UTC - Medisphere (customer): We are seeing missing transcripts for several patient sessions. This is urgent due to audits. Please advise.
2026-03-10 10:04 UTC - Support (Asha Menon): Acknowledged. Escalating to SRE and starting incident response. Gathering request IDs and logs.
2026-03-10 11:30 UTC - SRE (Ethan Park): Located audit-emitter restart timeline and node snapshot with partial buffers. Initiating secure transfer of recovered artifacts.

2026-03-11 08:20 UTC - Support (Customer Success): Provided Medisphere with reconstructed artifacts for 9 of 11 affected sessions. Remaining two sessions lacked finalization markers in buffer; next steps documented in follow-up tasks.
2026-03-12 14:05 UTC - Customer (Medisphere): Confirmed receipt of artifacts and acceptance of escalation credits. Requested formal RCA and changes to upgrade procedure.
investigation_notes: Root cause hypothesis: during leader handoff the emitter process encountered a TLS renegotiation timing window with the customer's S3 endpoint. The emitter restart logic includes an optimization to drop a resubscribe if it believes the consumer offset has been acknowledged; we observed an edge-case where acknowledgement was not observed due to a short-lived network reset.

SRE reproduced the restart sequence in staging by simulating TLS handshake timeouts combined with artificially delayed changefeed acks. The resubscribe skip path triggered when the emitter observed 'offset-confirmed' in memory but not in persistent ack ledger.
Telemetry gap: the control-plane metric emitter did not surface the missed-subscriptions as an alert (no 5xx). We relied on customer error reports to surface the window.
resolution_notes: Immediate: Replayed buffered audit events from node snapshots to customer's sink with idempotency and delivered artifacts for 9 of 11 sessions. Issued billing credit and made incident communication to Medisphere.

Fix deployed: emitter resubscribe logic patched to require persistent ack confirmation before dropping re-subscribe on restarts. Patch rolled to private-control-plane images and applied to eu-central canaries on 2026-03-11 03:40 UTC.
Guardrail: added pre-upgrade TLS sanity check and an explicit audit-emitter readiness gating step to the control-plane rolling upgrade job.
Monitoring: new metric 'audit_emitter_unconfirmed_restarts' created and alert rule added to trigger P1 when >1 event/10m.
followup_tasks: INT-331: Update upgrade runbook to require audit-emitter persistent ack before proceeding with leader handoff (owner: SRE team).
INT-4987: Add integration test in CI that simulates TLS handshake resets and verifies emitter resubscribe path (owner: infra/qa).
SUP-947001: Deliver final compliance package and signed artifact receipts to Medisphere (owner: Customer Success).
Security review: verify that recovered artifacts transfer complied with customer's encryption and access policies (owner: Security Ops).
Postmortem: publish incident write-up to Confluence with timeline, RCA, and follow-ups by 2026-03-17 (owner: Incident Commander).
